items.front: The seven SI base units?
items.back: Metre, kilogram, second, ampere, kelvin, mole, candela. Newton/joule/watt/pascal are derived.
items.examPoint: Units & measurement — SI base units & derived quantities
items.source: BIPM SI base units

items.front: Scalar vs vector — which of distance, displacement, speed, velocity?
items.back: Scalars: distance, speed. Vectors: displacement, velocity, acceleration, force (have direction).
items.examPoint: Motion — speed, velocity, acceleration & equations of motion
items.source: NCERT Science Class 9

items.front: Newton's three laws in one line each?
items.back: 1st = inertia; 2nd = F = ma (rate of change of momentum); 3rd = equal & opposite forces on DIFFERENT bodies.
items.examPoint: Newton's laws of motion, inertia & momentum
items.source: NCERT Science Class 9

items.front: Where is g greatest, and what is it on the Moon?
items.back: g is greater at the poles than the equator (~9.83 vs 9.78); on the Moon g ≈ 1/6 of Earth's. Weight zero at Earth's centre.
items.examPoint: Gravitation — universal law, acceleration due to gravity (g) & mass vs weight
items.source: NCERT Science Class 9

items.front: Archimedes' principle & when a body floats?
items.back: Upthrust = weight of fluid displaced. A body floats if its average density < the fluid's. Pressure P = hρg.
items.examPoint: Fluids — pressure, density, buoyancy & Archimedes' principle (floating/sinking)
items.source: NCERT Science Class 9 — Gravitation

items.front: Converging vs diverging: lenses and mirrors?
items.back: Convex lens & concave mirror converge; concave lens & convex mirror diverge. Rear-view = convex mirror.
items.examPoint: Light — reflection, mirrors, refraction, lenses & dispersion
items.source: NCERT Science Class 10

items.front: Human audible range; infrasound vs ultrasound?
items.back: 20 Hz – 20,000 Hz. Infrasound < 20 Hz; ultrasound > 20 kHz (used in SONAR). Sound needs a medium.
items.examPoint: Sound — characteristics, speed, ultrasound, echo & SONAR
items.source: NCERT Science Class 9

items.front: Three modes of heat transfer — which works in vacuum?
items.back: Conduction (solids), convection (fluids), radiation (no medium — works in vacuum, e.g. Sun's heat).
items.examPoint: Heat — conduction, convection, radiation & specific/latent heat
items.source: NCERT Science Class 9

items.front: Is an electric fuse in series or parallel? Basis?
items.back: In SERIES in the live wire; melts on overload (heating effect of current). Ohm's law: V = IR.
items.examPoint: Electricity & magnetism — Ohm's law, circuits & electromagnetic induction
items.source: NCERT Science Class 10

items.front: Fission vs fusion — which powers reactors and which the Sun?
items.back: Fission (heavy nucleus splits) → nuclear reactors/atom bomb. Fusion (light nuclei combine) → the Sun/H-bomb.
items.examPoint: Modern physics — atomic structure, radioactivity, nuclear fission & fusion
items.source: NCERT Science Class 10

items.front: Element vs compound vs mixture — where does air fall?
items.back: Air = mixture; water/CO₂ = compounds; iron/oxygen = elements. Rusting is a chemical change.
items.examPoint: Matter — states, classification (element/compound/mixture) & physical vs chemical change
items.source: NCERT Science Class 9

items.front: Chemical names: baking soda, washing soda, bleaching powder, quicklime?
items.back: NaHCO₃, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O, CaOCl₂, CaO. Slaked lime = Ca(OH)₂; PoP = CaSO₄·½H₂O.
items.examPoint: Common compounds & their chemical names (baking soda, washing soda, bleaching powder)
items.source: NCERT Science Class 10

items.front: Only liquid metal; brass and bronze composition?
items.back: Mercury is the only liquid metal. Brass = Cu + Zn; bronze = Cu + Tin; steel = Fe + carbon.
items.source: NCERT Science Class 10

items.front: Largest gland; universal donor & recipient blood groups?
items.back: Liver is the largest gland. Universal donor = O-negative; universal recipient = AB. Nephron = kidney unit.
items.examPoint: Human systems — digestion, respiration, circulation & blood groups
items.source: NCERT Science Class 10

items.front: Vitamin deficiency diseases A, C, D, B1?
items.back: A → night blindness; C → scurvy; D → rickets; B1 → beriberi. Iron → anaemia; iodine → goitre.
items.source: NCERT Science Class 9

items.front: A body moves in a circle at steady speed. Is its velocity constant?
items.back: No — speed is constant but the direction keeps changing, so velocity changes.
items.examPoint: Motion — speed, velocity, acceleration & equations of motion
